newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsuzuka to meet Thai finance minister on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Mitsuzuka to meet Thai finance minister on Friday.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is planning to set up a meeting between the finance ministers of Japan and Thailand on Friday, July 18, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday.

Asked about the Asian currency crisis and what Japan plans to do to help resolve it, Mitsuzuka said: "We will keep a careful watch and keep in close contact (with the authorities). At the moment, I don't think the situation is as serious as some people say."
He added that he felt Thailand's move to a managed floating system for its currency will eventually lead to a stabilisation of the baht.
"The Thai finance minister is coming at the end of this week and we would like to consider timely and appropriate measures after listening to what he has to say," Mitsuzuka said.

Asked about a comment on Tuesday by Taku Yamasaki, who chairs the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's Policy Research Council, that Japan's corporate income tax should be cut by 2.5 percentage points, Mitsuzuka said that the comment reflected Yamasaki's personal views and that neither Mitsuzuka nor other finance ministry officials were discussing the issue with him.
"Regarding the corporate tax, our intention to broaden the tax base, while lowering the rate, has not changed," he said.
